question: A borrows a sum of ₹90,000 for 4 years at 5% simple interest. He lends it to B at 7% for 4 years at simple interest. What is his gain (in ₹)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net gain rate = Lending rate − Borrowing rate = 7% − 5% = 2% per year.

Total gain percentage over 4 years = 2% × 4 = 8%.

Total Gain = 8% of ₹90,000 = (8 ÷ 100) × 90,000 = ₹7,200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹90,000

Rate of borrowing (R₁) = 5% per annum

Rate of lending (R₂) = 7% per annum

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Gain = Interest Received − Interest Paid

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/23fd7a27e8765482f39d9a80d01620f4f1ffc248fd824e31e248206ac61f4fed.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest paid by A to the lender = (90,000 × 5 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ Interest paid by A = 900 × 20 = ₹18,000

⇒ Interest received by A from B = (90,000 × 7 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ Interest received by A = 900 × 28 = ₹25,200

⇒ Total Gain = Interest Received − Interest Paid

⇒ Total Gain = 25,200 − 18,000 = ₹7,200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is the principal, R is the rate of interest per annum, and T is the time in years.

Difference in Simple Interest

When the principal and the time period are the same, the difference in Simple Interest is directly proportional to the difference in their rates: ΔSI = [P × T × (R₁ − R₂)] ÷ 100.

Simple vs Compound Interest

For the first year, both Simple Interest and Compound Interest (compounded annually) are exactly identical. From the second year onwards, Compound Interest grows faster as it calculates interest on the accumulated interest as well.
